metadata.description: AI/ML terminology with definitions for technical learning

vocabulary.definition: Field enabling computers to perform tasks requiring human intelligence like learning, perception, and decision-making.
Subset of AI where computers learn patterns from data without explicit programming.
Advanced ML using multi-layered neural networks to analyze complex data, inspired by human brain structure.
AI models trained on vast text datasets to understand and generate human-like language (e.g., GPT, Claude, Gemini).
Computing systems with interconnected nodes processing information, foundation of modern AI.
Trained algorithm that makes predictions or generates outputs; the result of training on data.
Process of teaching model by exposing it to data so it learns patterns.
When trained model makes predictions on new data it hasn't seen before.
Adjustable values in model that get tuned during training to improve performance (e.g., "7B parameters").
Further training pre-trained model on specific dataset to specialize for particular task.
Designing effective instructions to optimize AI model outputs.
Input text or instruction given to AI model to generate response.
Maximum amount of text model can process in single interaction.
Smallest unit of text model processes; models have token limits.
When AI generates false or fabricated information confidently.
Combining information retrieval with generation to ground responses in real documents (RAG).
Numerical representation of text capturing semantic meaning for similarity searches.
Database storing embeddings for efficient semantic search.
Application Programming Interface allowing programs to communicate with AI services.
URL or interface where applications send requests to get AI predictions.
Autonomous system that can reason, plan, use tools, and take actions to achieve goals.
AI systems operating autonomously with minimal supervision to accomplish complex workflows.
Popular framework for building LLM applications with tools for chaining prompts and managing workflows.
Agent's ability to invoke external functions or APIs to accomplish tasks.
Multiple specialized AI agents collaborating to handle complex tasks.
Technique where model shows step-by-step reasoning before final answer.
Managing coordination between multiple agents working together.
Collection of data used to train or test models.
Data used to teach model patterns and behaviors.
Separate data evaluating model during training to tune settings.
Hold-out data assessing final model performance after training.
Training on labeled data where correct answers are provided.
Finding patterns in unlabeled data without predefined outputs.
Learning through trial and error with rewards for good decisions.
When model memorizes training data too well and performs poorly on new data.
Changes in data distribution over time affecting model performance.
Configuration setting chosen before training (unlike parameters learned during training).
Methods making AI decisions transparent and understandable to humans (XAI).
Model providing outputs without revealing decision-making process.
Systematic errors or unfair outcomes in AI systems due to training data or design.
Ensuring AI treats different groups equitably without discrimination.
Method assigning importance scores to features explaining predictions.
Technique explaining individual predictions by approximating with simpler local models.
Measure showing which inputs most influence model predictions.
Moral principles guiding responsible AI development and deployment.
Practices ensuring AI is safe, fair, transparent, and accountable.
Practices streamlining ML model development, deployment, and maintenance in production.
Making trained model available for use in production environments.
Tracking model performance and behavior in production.
Automated workflow connecting multiple steps (data processing, training, deployment).
Automatically retraining models with new data to maintain accuracy.
Comparing two model versions by exposing each to different user groups.
Centralized storage for managing and versioning trained models.
Repository for storing and serving features used by ML models.
Tracking different iterations of models for reproducibility and rollback.
Processing multiple prediction requests together rather than individually.
Providing immediate predictions as requests arrive.
Microsoft's cloud platform for full ML lifecycle.
AWS service for building, training, deploying ML models.
Google's unified AI platform.
Open-source platform for managing ML lifecycle including experiments and deployment.
Unified analytics platform for data processing and ML.
Platform for experiment tracking and model collaboration.
AI coding assistant generating code from natural language.
Tool for packaging applications in portable containers.
Platform automating deployment and scaling of containerized applications.
Enabling computers to understand and generate human language (NLP).
Breaking text into smaller units (tokens) for processing.
Determining emotional tone in text.
Identifying people, places, organizations in text.
Categorizing text into predefined groups.
Automatically translating between languages.
Creating human-like text from prompts or data.
Enabling computers to interpret visual information.
Categorizing images into classes.
Identifying and locating objects in images.
Rectangle drawn around objects to indicate location.
Identifying individuals from facial features.
Creating new images using AI (e.g., DALL-E, Stable Diffusion).
Neural network architecture using attention mechanisms, foundation of modern LLMs.
Component allowing models to focus on relevant input parts.
Architecture with separate components for processing inputs and generating outputs.
Network using convolution operations, effective for images (CNN).
Network processing sequential data by maintaining memory (RNN).
AI creating new content including text, images, code, audio.
Model generating images by gradually removing noise (e.g., Stable Diffusion).
AI processing multiple data types simultaneously (text, images, audio).
Reducing numerical precision to decrease model size and increase speed.
Reducing model size while maintaining performance.
Training smaller model to mimic larger model's behavior.
Low-Rank Adaptation - efficient method for fine-tuning models with minimal parameter updates.
Removing unnecessary parameters from models to reduce size.
Number of examples processed together during training.
How much model adjusts during each training step.
Graphics Processing Unit - hardware accelerating AI computations.
Ensuring AI operates without causing unintended harm.
Attack manipulating model by inserting malicious instructions.
Blocking harmful or inappropriate outputs.
Requiring human validation at critical decision points.
Adversarial testing to find system vulnerabilities.
Safety mechanisms preventing unintended agent behaviors.
Recorded history of system actions for accountability.
Documentation providing transparency about model capabilities and limitations.
Percentage of correct predictions.
Of predicted positives, how many were actually correct.
Of actual positives, how many were correctly identified.
Balance between precision and recall.
Time delay between request and response.
Amount of work processed in given time.
Measure of model error during training that gets minimized.
Table showing correct and incorrect predictions by category.
Delivering computing services over internet.
Processing data near source rather than centralized cloud.
Packaging applications with dependencies in isolated containers.
Running code without managing underlying servers.
Distributing requests across multiple servers.
Entry point managing API requests and routing.
Designing applications as independent, modular services.
Continuous Integration/Continuous Deployment - automated testing and release process.
Interactive environment for writing code with documentation.
Tracking changes to code over time (e.g., Git).
Recording ML experiments with parameters and results.
File or object produced during ML process (weights, configs).
Saved state during training allowing resumption if interrupted.
Simple model or benchmark for comparison.
Initial training on large dataset before specialization.
LLM enhanced for logical thinking and multi-step problem solving (e.g., o1, o3).
Process where agents autonomously plan, execute, and refine tasks.
AI systems interacting with and learning from physical world.
Writing code by describing problems in natural language, AI generates implementation.
Compact models offering efficiency with lower resource requirements.
Developing efficient AI prioritizing reduced computation and energy use.
Embedding markers identifying AI-generated content.
Unexpected capabilities arising from complex AI system interactions.
Standard enabling agents to connect with external tools uniformly (MCP).
Communication standard for agents across platforms (A2A).
